cues.en: Instructor: Now that you have gained some experience working with histograms, creating histograms, and interpreting histograms for different kinds of data, different distributions of data,
cues.zh: 既然已經有使用、建立、解讀不同資料與分布直方圖的經驗，

cues.en: it is time to learn the rules or actually guidelines for determining an appropriate number of bins to use for the histogram.
cues.zh: 該學習決定適當區間數的規則，或者說指引。

cues.en: And of course, when I say bins, I'm not referring to these things.
cues.zh: 當然，說bins不是指這些東西。

cues.en: I'm referring to the discretization of the data.
cues.zh: 是指資料的離散化。

cues.en: So how you come up with a bunch of boundaries for putting the data into in order to create the histogram.
cues.zh: 如何決定一系列邊界，把資料放進去，建立直方圖。

cues.en: So not these bins.
cues.zh: 不是這些箱子。

cues.en: By the way, I apologize for these awful jokes.
cues.zh: 順帶為爛笑話道歉。

cues.en: I don't know what I was thinking when I made these slides.
cues.zh: 不知道當時做投影片在想什麼。

cues.en: Anyway, so this is a copy of a slide you've seen before when I first introduced you to histograms in the previous section.
cues.zh: 總之，這是上一節首次介紹直方圖時，看過的投影片。

cues.en: So the idea here was that these are exactly the same data sets.
cues.zh: 概念是，資料集完全相同。

cues.en: So all of these, these three histograms come from exactly the same set of numbers.
cues.zh: 三個直方圖，都來自同一組數。

cues.en: I'm just using a different number of bins to show the histogram.
cues.zh: 只是區間數不同。

cues.en: Now, in this case, it was really clear that four bins is too few, 700 bins is too many, and 30 bins seems reasonable.
cues.zh: 很明顯，四個太少、七百太多、三十似乎合理。

cues.en: But why 30 bins? Why not 32 bins or 47 bins?
cues.zh: 但為什麼三十？不是三十二，或四十七？

cues.en: Why 30 in particular?
cues.zh: 為什麼特別三十？

cues.en: Well, in this case, that was actually just kind of arbitrary.
cues.zh: 其實當時有點任意。

cues.en: I just picked this number.
cues.zh: 只是選了這個數。

cues.en: But it turns out that there are mathematical ways, there are mathematical guidelines to help you decide an appropriate number of bins for a particular data dataset.
cues.zh: 但有數學方法、指引，協助替特定資料集，選適當區間數。

cues.en: Now, in general, there is two ways to come up with a number of bins, and that's also called the K parameter for histogram.
cues.zh: 一般有兩種方式，區間數也叫直方圖的K參數。

cues.en: So in this case, K would be 4, 30, and 700.
cues.zh: 這裡K分別是4、30、700。

cues.en: So either you can justify K directly, and there are some methods where we just plug in a formula and that gives us the result for K, the number of bins.
cues.zh: 可以直接決定K，有些方法直接套公式，得到K、區間數。

cues.en: And there are other methods or other algorithms that actually recommend an H, which is the bin width.
cues.zh: 其他方法、演算法，則建議H，也就是區間寬度。

cues.en: So this would be how wide a particular bin is, what is the range of values that's covered, that's spanned by one specific bin.
cues.zh: 一個區間多寬、涵蓋多少數值範圍。

cues.en: And from there you would apply this formula to obtain a number of bins.
cues.zh: 再用這個公式，得到區間數。

cues.en: So this is the maximum value of X, the largest value in X minus the min of X, so the smallest value in X.
cues.zh: X最大值，減X最小值。

cues.en: Essentially, this is just the total range of the data divided by the width of each bin.
cues.zh: 基本上，資料總範圍，除以每個區間寬度。

cues.en: And this is unlikely, this fraction is unlikely to be a whole number, but of course we need K to be a positive integer because yeah, it doesn't make sense to have 17.32 bins.
cues.zh: 比值不太可能是整數，但K必須是正整數，因為17.32個區間沒意義。

cues.en: So therefore we apply the ceiling function.
cues.zh: 所以使用向上取整函式。

cues.en: That's what these kind of weird looking L shape or like half like two thirds of a square bracket here.
cues.zh: 這些奇怪的L形，像三分之二個方括號，

cues.en: This indicates the ceiling function.
cues.zh: 表示向上取整。

cues.en: The ceiling function is like rounding to the nearest integer, except you're always rounding up.
cues.zh: 類似取最接近整數，但永遠向上。

cues.en: So taking the ceiling of the number 2.001 is actually the number three.
cues.zh: 2.001向上取整，其實是3。

cues.en: Okay, so the point is you can either specify the number of bins directly or you specify the bin width.
cues.zh: 所以能直接指定區間數，或指定區間寬度。

cues.en: And from the bin width you can compute the number of bins.
cues.zh: 從寬度，就能算數量。

cues.en: Alright, so I'm gonna walk you through a couple of different guidelines.
cues.zh: 介紹幾個指引。

cues.en: These are actually often termed rules, but they're not really rules per se.
cues.zh: 常叫規則，但其實不是必須遵守的規定。

cues.en: You don't have to follow them.
cues.zh: 不一定要遵循。

cues.en: These are really just suggestions.
cues.zh: 真的只是建議。

cues.en: Okay, so one is called Sturges' rule or Sturges' guideline.
cues.zh: 一個叫Sturges規則、指引。

cues.en: And that allows us to specify K directly.
cues.zh: 直接指定K。

cues.en: And this is the formula.
cues.zh: 這是公式。

cues.en: So we take the log, base 2 of N.
cues.zh: 取N以2為底的對數。

cues.en: And N is the number of data points you have.
cues.zh: N是資料點數。

cues.en: So then you take the ceiling of that number because this is unlikely to be a whole number.
cues.zh: 再向上取整，因為不太可能剛好是整數。

cues.en: And then you add 1.
cues.zh: 接著加1。

cues.en: And honestly, I don't know how Sturges derived this plus 1.
cues.zh: 老實說，不知道Sturges如何推導這個加1。

cues.en: I don't know why that factors there, but that is the formula for the Sturges recommendation for the number of histogram bins.
cues.zh: 不知道因子為何在這裡，但這就是Sturges建議區間數的公式。

cues.en: So you can see that the number of bins will increase as the number of data points you have increases.
cues.zh: 資料點增加，區間數也增加。

cues.en: And you can see also that this is a non-linear function.
cues.zh: 也能看出，這是非線性函數。

cues.en: So remember the logarithm goes up like this, it goes up pretty steeply in the beginning for small numbers.
cues.zh: 記得對數這樣上升，小數值時，一開始很陡。

cues.en: And as X, or in this case N, as you get further and further to the right, the increase slows down.
cues.zh: x，這裡是N，越往右，增加越慢。

cues.en: So you're gonna have a larger and larger and larger N is not necessarily giving you a much larger number of histogram bins.
cues.zh: 所以N越來越大，不一定帶來大很多的直方圖區間數。

cues.en: So this is one advantage of Sturges' rule.
cues.zh: 這是Sturges規則的一個優點。

cues.en: It depends on the data count.
cues.zh: 依賴資料數量。

cues.en: So as the data gets larger, the number of bins gets larger.
cues.zh: 資料越多，區間越多。

cues.en: Next we have the Freedman-Diaconis rule, which is sometimes just abbreviated as FD, the FD rule, the FD recommendation.
cues.zh: 接著Freedman–Diaconis規則，有時簡稱FD，FD規則、建議。

cues.en: And here we're not specifying K directly.
cues.zh: 這裡不直接指定K。

cues.en: Instead we're specifying H, which is the width of the bins from which we can compute the number of bins as I showed in the previous slide.
cues.zh: 而是H，區間寬度，再照前一張公式算數量。

cues.en: Now, I don't know where this formula comes from or how Freedman and Diaconis derived this rule, but when you look at it for a minute, you can see that it, it's a pretty sensible rule.
cues.zh: 不知道公式來源，或他們如何推導，但看一會兒，會覺得相當合理。

cues.en: So it is the IQR, which is the inner quartile range.
cues.zh: 取IQR，也就是四分位距。

cues.en: Remember, this is the difference in data values between quartile 1 and quartile 3.
cues.zh: 記得，是第一與第三四分位數的資料值之差。

cues.en: In other words, this is the range that contains 50% of your data and that's divided by the cube root of N.
cues.zh: 也就是涵蓋50%資料的範圍，除以N的立方根。

cues.en: So again, this is something that's going to grow with N, but it's not gonna grow as fast as N is growing.
cues.zh: 這也隨N增加，但沒有N增加得快。

cues.en: So we can think about what's going to happen with this bin width here as the quartile range gets larger or smaller.
cues.zh: 想想四分位距變大、變小，寬度會怎樣。

cues.en: So as IQR gets larger, which means your data have more and more spread, there's more dispersion in the data, then this ratio will get larger,
cues.zh: IQR越大，資料越分散，這個比值越大，

cues.en: which means that the total number of bins will get larger, or sorry, the total bin size will get larger.
cues.zh: 表示區間總數越大，抱歉，是區間大小越大。

cues.en: And that means that the number of bins will start to decrease.
cues.zh: 所以區間數開始減少。

cues.en: And that's because H is in the denominator of the formula to compute K, the number of bins.
cues.zh: 因為計算K時，H在分母。

cues.en: And now we can also think about what happens as N grows.
cues.zh: 也能想想N增加的情況。

cues.en: So as N gets larger and larger, then this fraction is gonna get smaller and smaller, which means the bins width is getting smaller,
cues.zh: N越大，比值越小，區間寬度越小，

cues.en: which means we end up with a larger number of bins following the formula from the previous slide.
cues.zh: 根據前一張公式，區間數就越大。

cues.en: So the FD rule is pretty interesting because it depends both on the data count and on the data spread.
cues.zh: FD規則很有意思，因為同時取決於資料數量與分散程度。

cues.en: Okay, and then finally, actually this is not really finally, these are just the three that I'm going to discuss here because these are the three most commonly used guidelines.
cues.zh: 最後，其實不真正是最後，只是這裡討論最常見的三個指引。

cues.en: If you look up online, you'll probably find there must be like half a dozen or maybe 10 of these different recommendations for how to choose the number of bins.
cues.zh: 上網查，大概至少有六到十種選區間數的不同建議。

cues.en: So anyway, this third one is to just arbitrarily choose some number of bins that seems appropriate to you for that particular data set.
cues.zh: 第三個，是任意挑一個你覺得適合資料集的數。

cues.en: And generally somewhere around 30, 40, 50, that tends to be a pretty good number.
cues.zh: 一般三十、四十、五十左右，往往不錯。

cues.en: Now, I don't mean to say anything bad about this arbitrary selection, it often works out pretty well.
cues.zh: 不是說任意挑不好，經常效果很好。

cues.en: You can use your intuition in many cases and get at a pretty decent histogram just by picking a number and playing around a little bit.
cues.zh: 很多情況能用直覺，挑個數、稍微調整，就得到不錯直方圖。

cues.en: Nonetheless, these are the two most commonly used guidelines.
cues.zh: 不過，這是兩個最常用的指引。

cues.en: And this one, the Freedman-Diaconis rule, this I think is the best one.
cues.zh: Freedman–Diaconis，我認為最好。

cues.en: It's the most common choice and it's better than Sturges' I think, because it incorporates both the, not only just the raw number of data points,
cues.zh: 最常選，我認為比Sturges好，因為不只納入原始資料點數，

cues.en: but also the characteristics of the data.
cues.zh: 也納入資料特性。

cues.en: So the features of the dataset are guiding the number of histogram bins.
cues.zh: 資料集特徵，會引導區間數選擇。

cues.en: Okay, so you might have noticed that for all three of these formulas, what we're doing is either specifying one bin width or one number of bins,
cues.zh: 可能注意到，三個公式都只指定一個區間寬度，或一個區間數，

cues.en: and that is constant for the entire histogram.
cues.zh: 整張直方圖固定。

cues.en: Maybe you're wondering if it's possible to have different histogram bins within a dataset.
cues.zh: 可能好奇，一個資料集中，能否有不同區間。

cues.en: So within one histogram plot, different bins have different sizes.
cues.zh: 同一張直方圖，各區間大小不同。

cues.en: Now, in theory that's possible you end up with something that looks like this.
cues.zh: 理論上可以，會得到這種樣子。

cues.en: It almost, you know, is a little bit perceptually deceiving because it kind of looks like these bars are all equally wide, but some of them are hidden behind other ones,
cues.zh: 視覺上有點誤導，好像所有長條一樣寬，只是有些藏在其他後面，

cues.en: like this bar could go out to here, but actually that's not what's happening.
cues.zh: 例如這個可能延伸到這裡，但其實不是。

cues.en: Each of these bins has a different width.
cues.zh: 每個區間寬度都不同。

cues.en: So I think this looks pretty cool, but looks a little bit like a abstracted cityscape.
cues.zh: 我覺得很酷，有點像抽象城市景觀。

cues.en: But don't do this in practice it gets really weird.
cues.zh: 但實務上別這樣做，會很奇怪。

cues.en: It's hard to interpret the data when the bins have different sizes.
cues.zh: 區間大小不同，資料難解讀。

cues.en: And when you get to the stage of quantifying histogram characteristics, then this also becomes a quite a bit of a headache.
cues.zh: 進一步量化直方圖特徵時，也很頭痛。

cues.en: So, you know, if you're making like something interesting to print out on a T-shirt, then yeah, go for it.
cues.zh: 如果想印在T恤上，當有趣圖案，可以。

cues.en: It looks pretty cool.
cues.zh: 看起來很酷。

cues.en: But in practice for statistics, just stick to fixed width histogram bins.
cues.zh: 但實際統計，還是用固定寬度。

cues.en: All right, so in this video I discussed bins.
cues.zh: 這部影片談了區間。

cues.en: I showed you how to create the number of bins based on the bin width, and I introduced you to three principles
cues.zh: 展示如何由寬度得到區間數，並介紹三個原則，

cues.en: for choosing an appropriate number of bins for a given dataset.
cues.zh: 為特定資料集選合適區間數。

cues.en: And just as a reminder, it was the Freedman-Diaconis rule or the FD rule that is the most commonly used, and I think it's the most commonly used because it's really the best one.
cues.zh: 提醒，Freedman–Diaconis、FD規則最常用，我想是因為最好。

cues.en: It works well in pretty much all cases.
cues.zh: 幾乎所有情況都適用。
